_comment: Model and decoding parameters for the intention task. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF
TRUTH: cli.py has no --model / --max-new-tokens / --temperature / --top-p /
--top-k / --do-sample / --enable-thinking / --max-video-frames flags any more, so
change a run by editing here and resubmitting. A run's settings are then something
that can be read, diffed and committed rather than reconstructed from an sbatch
line, and they are recorded into every result file's __summary__.
It is task-scoped on purpose. Another task wanting a different frame budget or
token cap gets its own model_config.json beside its own prompt config rather than
editing this one; models/config.py reads whichever file the task hands it.
'defaults' applies to every backend; a backend's 'generation' overrides it. Backend
names must match models/registry.py BACKEND_MODULES. Any key starting with _ is a
comment, and an unknown key is a hard error rather than a shrug -- a mistyped
'temprature' that was silently ignored is the worst thing that can happen here,
because the run looks configured and is not.
model_id   weights path or hub id, and the ONLY place it is set. No model tensors
live in this repo; this is where the provided path goes. The two
/REPLACE_ME/... values below are placeholders and will fail the
startup check by design -- an absolute path that is not a directory
is refused before the manifest is even read. Keep replacements
absolute: a relative value is treated as a hub id and skips that
check entirely.
null falls back to the backend module's own DEFAULT_MODEL_PATH.
load       keyword arguments handed to the backend's constructor.
generation decoding overrides on top of 'defaults'.
extra      backend-only knobs; setting one a backend does not support is refused
up front, which is what --enable-thinking used to check by hand.
FRAME SAMPLING is one policy for every backend, in 'defaults' below:
video_fps         target rate. 2.0 is Qwen's own upstream default, so an
unconfigured run samples what that backend would have chosen.
min_video_frames  floor. 4 is Qwen's FPS_MIN_FRAMES; short clips land here.
max_video_frames  ceiling, and the guard against a long clip blowing up memory.
models/media_io.py frames_at_fps resolves them once -- n = duration * fps, clamped,
rounded down to even -- and every backend is handed that exact count. Frame count is
the largest controllable confound when two models are compared, so it is decided
here rather than by each package's own constants.
temperature/top_p/top_k only take effect when do_sample is true.
enable_thinking is Gemma's reasoning mode, and the capability check refuses it
on a backend that does not advertise 'thinking' -- so moving this line to the
qwen7b section below fails at startup rather than being dropped on the floor.
use_audio_in_video would additionally feed the video's own audio track; this
task already supplies audio as separate WAV parts (the participant's own track
and the conversation-floor mix), so it is off.
disable_talker drops the speech tower, which this task never uses.
attn_implementation is sdpa, and leaving it unset is NOT the same as eager:
unset means whatever transformers decides, and on the 4.52 in the qwen image
that was eager for every tower even though the top-level config reported sdpa.
Eager materialises a full N-by-N attention matrix per layer, and the vision
tower attends over patches -- four per visual token -- so its matrix is sixteen
times the one the token count suggests. A measured run asked for a single
31.64 GiB tensor and died on a 96 GB card.
flash_attention_2 is NOT the one to reach for: the RTX PRO 6000 is Blackwell
(compute 12.x) and upstream flash-attn targets older architectures.
After changing this, check the job log's '[INFO] Qwen attention (requested ...)'
line: a request the model class does not implement leaves the towers on eager
without raising.
